title: JavaScript Modules Core Check
description: Check your understanding of ES modules, import/export syntax, default and named exports, browser modules, re-exports, and dynamic imports.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A JavaScript file that can import and export code
A function that must return an object

questions.explanation: A module is a JavaScript file with its own scope that can share code through exports and use code through imports.

questions.prompt: Which keyword makes a function available to other modules?
questions.explanation: `export` makes a value available for import by other modules.
Named exports are imported with curly braces and the exported name.
Default exports are imported without curly braces.

questions.prompt: How many default exports can one module have?
questions.explanation: A module may have no default export or one default export, but not multiple default exports.

questions.prompt: Which import collects all named exports into one object?
questions.explanation: `import * as math` creates a namespace object containing the module's named exports.

questions.prompt: What should a browser script tag include if the JavaScript file uses `import` statements?
questions.explanation: Browser ES modules are loaded with `<script type="module" src="..."></script>`.

questions.prompt: Which local import path is usually correct from the same folder in browser modules?
questions.explanation: Relative local imports commonly start with `./` or `../`.

options.text: An import that runs a module without importing named values
An import that always fails silently
An import that only works with arrays
An import that creates a default export

questions.explanation: `import "./setup.js"` runs the module for its side effects without importing bindings.

options.text: A Promise for a module object

questions.explanation: Dynamic `import()` is asynchronous and returns a Promise that resolves to the module object.
`export *` re-exports named exports. It does not automatically re-export a default export.

questions.prompt: What is one benefit of modules compared with old global script files?

options.text: Modules make all variables global automatically
Modules avoid global scope pollution and make dependencies explicit
Modules remove the need for functions
Modules only run in HTML, never in Node.js

questions.explanation: Modules have their own scope and use explicit imports/exports, which reduces accidental global dependencies.
